author: Yelena Mandenberg
title: Pastor accused of stabbing girlfriend's ex and hiding out in church - NewsBreak
text:
By Yelena Mandenberg ,
1 hours ago A Minnesota pastor was charged for allegedly stabbing his girlfriend's ex over a "confrontation over some tools and a receipt," according to police.
According to court documents, Terrence Philip Walker Sr., 61, of Prior Lake, was charged with second-degree felony assault with a dangerous weapon. Walker Sr. is known as a pastor at Morning Star Missionary Baptist Church in St. Paul.
St. Paul police say they were called to a house in 1100 block of Marion Street at 10:45 on June 25. When they arrived, they found a 39-year-old "man without a shirt bleeding heavily and pressing his clothing against a deep abdominal wound that exposed internal tissue." He was taken to Regions Hospital and rushed into surgery.

Court records say the stabbing followed an argument over tools and a receipt. The man, who shares children with Walker’s longtime girlfriend, told investigators he went to the home to pick up belongings he had been storing in the garage.
He said he believed some of his tools had been pawned and asked for receipts, adding that he had seen surveillance video showing Walker and the woman removing some of the tools.
Walker and the church did not reply to requests for comment.
According to the criminal complaint, a woman at the residence told officers the two men were arguing on the front steps when she saw Walker make a swinging motion with his arms.
The victim’s daughter said the men had their foreheads pressed together when she heard what sounded like a slash, then saw her father bleeding. She reported that Walker then tried to strike him again multiple times as her mother stepped in to try to stop it.
Walker, however, told police a different version of events, the complaint said. He claimed the man showed up banging on the door, yelling insults and making threats, including saying he had a gun in his car. Walker said the man grabbed his shoulder and threw a punch as Walker was walking away, and he responded by pulling a knife from his pocket.
When officers asked him to produce the weapon, Walker indicated a razor blade police recovered that was used for trimming beards, according to the complaint. The injured man told investigators he was stabbed with a long, serrated hunting knife and said Walker’s account was not accurate.
Walker is due back in court on July 23 in Ramsey County District Court.
